title: What I built: real scans, saved cleanup and software checks
instructions: Browse at your own pace; all feedback is optional. Comment beside any item, then use Submit review to send your comments to the agent. Save draft keeps unfinished comments for later but does not submit them. Dotted-underlined terms explain the AI-written prose; original OCR and proposed text stay plain. This is a requested progress walkthrough, not a mandatory grading round or another run-approval request. No real AI study was launched. No answer is needed for unrelated offline work to continue.

evidence.label: 1 · What changed, and what you can comment on
evidence.text:
This is a progress walkthrough you asked to see. No new AI study has run. You can inspect real source images, unchanged raw OCR, a saved fixed-rule cleanup proposal, and software checks using a fake server.

The fixed-rule sample covered 18 paragraphs in seven units: five selected passages, one per volume, plus two previously seen failure cases. It proposed six word joins across those 18 paragraphs. These are proposals, not six verified corrections.

The runner now saves exact requests and responses, keeps proposed readings separate from original OCR, and refuses incomplete or mismatched results. The full software gate passed 846 tests. That count does not measure historical accuracy.

Every card has its own optional note box. Nothing here asks you to reapprove the run. You can leave comments on any item and submit them, or simply browse.

evidence.label: 5 · What goes into a future AI request, and what must come back
evidence.text:
The request builder now packages the selected scan, original OCR, saved rule changes and inspection signals together. A single productive request is intended to cover every assigned word, including names, numbers, punctuation, repeated lines, bracketed cues and text that was not flagged.

The required response contains a full proposed reading, an exact list of edits and remaining uncertainties. The software checks that applying those edits recreates the proposed reading exactly. An audit of an earlier saved proposal has a separate response format and cannot silently rewrite that proposal.

These are implemented software requirements. The seven real requests are not yet ready to send, and there are no new real model outputs to show. The next card shows the invented server example actually used to test the connection.

evidence.label: 6 · Actual connection test: invented text, fake response
evidence.text:
Invented input:
By Mr. Example.

Prepared fake-server output:
By Mr. Example.

The fake server returned a prepared answer saying no change was found. The runner saved the original response, checked its required fields and exported a separate unreviewed proposal. Reopening the completed job reused the saved result without another request.

This tested software plumbing with invented text and a white test image. No language model read a historical page. A valid response format does not establish a correct reading.

evidence.label: 7 · Interruption checks: keep the result, avoid a duplicate request
evidence.text:
In four separate fake-server cases, the parent process was deliberately killed after different save steps: after the raw HTTP response was saved, after the journal saved it but before the stop receipt, after the raw result, and after the final result.

A new process resumed each case successfully. Each case retained exactly one request. The saved response was reused rather than asking again.

Other checks refused stale runtime observations, incomplete image/token evidence, an invented readiness claim and a partial response that happened to look like valid JSON. Invalid text encoding preserves the original bytes. Cancellation tests checked that a delayed worker could not send a late request.

These are bounded fake-server checks. They do not prove the installed AI model stops within the real time limit.

evidence.label: 8 · What still needs doing before the small AI study
evidence.text:
Two selected scan crops, S3 and S4, remain missing after the recorded timeouts. We have five saved images for the seven selected units; no replacement passages were slipped in.

We still need genuine native preprocessing evidence: how the installed backend turns this exact text and image into model input. A text-only token count is insufficient. One earlier illustrative image-grid calculation was over the candidate input limit; it was not an actual backend measurement. The limits have not been raised.

The selected real backend also needs compatibility and stopping evidence. No trusted launch clearance is recorded. Your existing approval is preserved; these are engineering checks, not a request to approve again.

The next planned task investigates the installed preprocessing path without generating a model response. The study remains at most seven sequential requests, zero automatic retries, with a 30-minute whole-session ceiling. Comments here are optional and do not block unrelated offline work.
